content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted and passes all quality checks. Per our Spec-Driven Development workflow, **this is the first review gate** — please review the spec before we plan or write any code.

- **Spec file**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Quality checklist**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md` (all items pass, no open clarifications)

## Summary of what I've specified

**Bookmark Manager** — a single-user web app to save and manage bookmarks.

**User stories (prioritized):**
1. **Save a bookmark** (P1) — add a link + optional title; auto-derive a title when none given.
2. **Browse, search & reopen** (P1) — list bookmarks, search by keyword, open the original page.
3. **Edit & delete** (P2) — correct or remove bookmarks, with delete confirmation.
4. **Organize with tags** (P3) — label bookmarks and filter by tag.

**12 functional requirements** covering saving, validation, persistence, listing, search, edit, delete, duplicate handling, tags, and empty/no-result states.

**Key entities:** Bookmark, Tag.

**Success criteria** are measurable and technology-agnostic (e.g., save in under 15s; find one of 100+ in under 10s; 100% retention across restarts).

**Notable scope decisions I assumed** (flagged in the Assumptions section — please confirm or correct):
- **Single-user, no authentication** in v1.
- **Local storage only** — no external sync or browser-extension import.
- **Desktop web browser** target; mobile layouts later.
- **http/https links only**; auto title-fetch is best-effort.

## Your options at this gate
- ✅ **Approve** the spec as-is → I proceed to `speckit-plan`.
- ✏️ **Request changes** (add/remove requirements, adjust scope or priorities) → I update the spec.
- ❓ **Clarify** — if anything feels ambiguous, I can run `speckit-clarify` to work through structured questions.

How would you like to proceed?

I’d like the specification expanded before planning.

Saving the same address should take me to the existing bookmark so I can update it, rather than merely warning me. When saving, I also expect the app to collect the page title, description, site icon, and preview image when available, while letting me edit the title and description.

I also need the specification to cover:

- Descriptions and notes, including formatted notes
- Suggestions from existing tags while entering tags
- Search across titles, descriptions, notes, addresses, and tags, without caring about capitalization
- Exact phrases, `#tag` searches, and combinations such as AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses
- Read-later/read status and a separate unread view
- Archiving as a reversible action, with archived items excluded from normal browsing and search
- Selecting several bookmarks—or everything matching the current search or filter—for actions such as tagging, read status, archiving, and deletion
- Sorting the bookmark list
- Saving reusable combinations of searches and included or excluded tags
- Preserving a local copy of a page, downloading the file itself for PDFs, plus an option to preserve it through the Internet Archive
- Importing and exporting standard browser bookmark files while retaining titles, tags, and dates
- Display preferences such as default sorting, number of items shown, and text size

The list should emphasize the title, description, tags, and site icon for easy reading. I’m happy with a single-user app without sign-in, and browser extensions can remain outside this version. Desktop-first is also fine. Please update the specification and its acceptance examples to make the behaviours and edge cases above clear, then bring it back for review.

The specification is expanded (revision 2) and still passes the quality checklist. We remain at the **spec review gate** — nothing has been planned or built yet.

- **Spec file**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Checklist**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md` (all pass, no open clarifications)

## What changed in revision 2

**Reworked behaviours:**
- **Duplicate save now opens the existing bookmark** for editing instead of just warning (US2, FR-007) — and if the match is archived, it offers to restore it (FR-008).
- **Metadata capture on save**: title, description, site icon, and preview image, best-effort, with title/description editable (US1, FR-002/003/005).

**Newly specified capabilities (each a prioritized, independently testable user story):**
- Short **description + separate formatted note** (US4, FR-009/010)
- **Tag suggestions** from existing tags, avoiding near-duplicates (US5, FR-012)
- **Advanced search** — case-insensitive across title/description/note/address/tags, plus exact phrases, `#tag`, and AND/OR/NOT with parentheses (US6, FR-017–020)
- **Read/unread status + separate unread view** (US7, FR-021/022)
- **Reversible archiving**, excluded from normal browsing/search (US8, FR-023/024)
- **Bulk actions** including "select all matching" a search (US9, FR-025–027)
- **Sorting** (US10, FR-028)
- **Saved views** — reusable search + included/excluded tags (US11, FR-029/030)
- **Page preservation** — local copy, PDF file download, and Internet Archive option (US12, FR-031–034)
- **Import/export** of standard browser bookmark files retaining titles, tags, dates (US13, FR-035–037)
- **Display preferences** — default sort, items per page, text size (US14, FR-039/040)

**List display** emphasizes title, description, tags, and site icon (FR-014). New entities added: **Saved View**, **Preserved Copy**, **Display Preferences**. Success criteria and edge cases updated (duplicate handling, archive leaks, normalization, malformed queries, large/malformed imports).

**Scope confirmed per your note:** single-user, no sign-in; browser extensions excluded; desktop-first.

## A few points I resolved with reasonable defaults (flagged in Assumptions — please confirm or adjust)
- **Address normalization** for duplicate detection (ignore trailing slash, host case, default port, stray fragment/tracking params) — exact rules finalized in planning.
- **New bookmarks default to unread.**
- **Notes** support a *basic, safe* formatting set (no embedded scripts).
- **Import merge**: an imported address that already exists merges rather than duplicates.

## Your options at this gate
- ✅ **Approve** → I proceed to `speckit-plan`.
- ✏️ **Request changes** → I revise the spec.
- ❓ **Clarify** the normalization/merge/notes defaults via `speckit-clarify` before planning.

How would you like to proceed?

This is much closer, but I’d like a few corrections before approving it:

- I need to be able to edit the bookmark’s address as well as its title, description, tags, and note.
- Selecting a visible tag on a bookmark should directly filter the list to bookmarks with that tag; requiring me to type a `#tag` search is not enough.
- Please state that words such as AND, OR, and NOT can still be searched as ordinary words when quoted.
- The locally preserved web page should be a self-contained HTML file. A PDF should still be stored as the PDF itself.

The unread default and safe note formatting are fine.

Please settle address matching in the specification rather than postponing it to planning. Ignoring host capitalization, a standard port, and an unimportant trailing slash seems reasonable. I would not automatically ignore every fragment or supposed tracking parameter, since either can sometimes identify different content; only remove one when it is known not to change the destination.

For imports, merging is fine, but please make the outcome predictable: retain the existing bookmark’s own title, description, note, read/archive state, and dates, while adding any imported tags it does not already have. Then return the revised specification for approval.

content:
That reference is fine (the unread default is genuinely in Assumptions). All six corrections are applied. The spec is now revision 3.

## Corrections applied (still at the spec review gate — nothing planned or built)

1. **Editable address** — US1 now covers editing title, description, **and address**; FR-003 updated; a new scenario handles editing an address into an existing one via the duplicate rules.
2. **Click-to-filter tags** — US3 scenario 3 and new **FR-014a**: clicking a tag shown on a bookmark immediately filters the list, no `#tag` typing needed.
3. **Quoted operators as plain words** — US6 scenario 5 and FR-018: `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` inside quotes are ordinary search text (e.g., `"rock and roll"`).
4. **Preserved page = self-contained HTML** — US12 and FR-031 specify a single self-contained HTML file with embedded assets; PDFs still stored as the PDF itself (FR-032).
5. **Address matching settled in the spec (new FR-041)** — same bookmark only when differing by host capitalization, a standard default port (80/443), or a single trailing slash. **Fragments and query parameters are treated as significant and never stripped wholesale**; a specific one may be ignored only if it's on a maintained known-harmless list. US2 scenarios, the edge case, and Assumptions all reflect this.
6. **Predictable import merge** — US13 scenario 2 and FR-036: an existing bookmark keeps its **own** title, description, note, read status, archive status, and dates; import **only adds tags it doesn't already have**; no duplicate; counts of added/merged/skipped reported.

Unread default and safe note formatting left as-is per your note.

- **Spec file**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Checklist**: all items still pass; no open `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers.

## Your options
- ✅ **Approve** → I proceed to `speckit-plan` (implementation plan).
- ✏️ **More changes** → I'll revise.

Shall I proceed to planning?
Yes, revision 3 now reflects the behavior I want. I approve the specification and the stated defaults. Please proceed to planning.

The implementation plan and Phase 0–1 design artifacts are complete. Constitution check passed (the project constitution is still an unfilled template, so I applied SDD's default gates — all pass). No extension hooks are configured.

We are now at the **plan review gate** — please review before I generate the task breakdown.

## Artifacts generated

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md` | Implementation plan, tech context, structure |
| `specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md` | Phase 0 — 10 key decisions with rationale/alternatives |
| `specs/001-bookmark-manager/data-model.md` | Phase 1 — entities, fields, rules |
| `specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/api.md` | Phase 1 — HTTP API contract, each endpoint mapped to FRs |
| `specs/001-bookmark-manager/quickstart.md` | Phase 1 — run + validation guide |

## Plan at a glance

**Stack** (driven by the runtime environment — Node 24, Chromium/Playwright, port 4000):
- **Node.js + Express**, one deployable serving a JSON API **and** a dependency-light static front end, listening on `0.0.0.0:4000`, started via `npm start`.
- **SQLite** (`better-sqlite3`) for storage; preserved copies saved as files under `data/preserved/`.
- **Playwright/Chromium** (pinned **1.61.0**) for best-effort metadata capture and self-contained-HTML preservation.
- **Custom search parser** for phrase / `#tag` / AND-OR-NOT-parentheses semantics (including "AND as a literal word when quoted"); SQLite may back word indexing.
- **HTML-subset sanitizer** for safe formatted notes.

**Key design decisions tied to your spec:**
- Duplicate matching enforced by a `url_key` unique column computed strictly per **FR-041** (host case, default port, single trailing slash only — fragments/query preserved).
- Import merge keeps the existing bookmark's own fields and only adds missing tags (**FR-036**).
- Preservation: self-contained HTML with inlined assets for pages; PDF stored verbatim; Internet Archive reference stored (**FR-031-034**).
- Every API endpoint in the contract is annotated with the FRs it satisfies.

**Testing:** `node:test` for services + API integration; a few Playwright e2e flows.

## Your options at this gate
- ✅ **Approve** → I proceed to `speckit-tasks` (dependency-ordered task breakdown).
- ✏️ **Adjust** the plan (e.g., different storage, framework, or structure).

Shall I proceed to tasks?

The overall approach is fine, but please correct two points before creating the task breakdown.

First, “select all matching” must use the complete view I am currently looking at—not just the search words or one tag. That includes all included and excluded tags, the unread or archive view, and any saved view. It should cover matching items on every page and show the correct affected count before deletion.

Second, because this is one user without sign-in, a browser session must not create a separate collection or separate settings. Bookmarks, saved views, and display preferences should still be there after restarting the app or returning in a new browser visit. A cookie may be used behind the scenes, but it should not divide the data into hidden session-specific profiles.

Once those points are reflected in the plan, I’m happy for you to proceed to the task breakdown.

## Specification Analysis Report

| ID | Category | Severity | Location(s) | Summary | Recommendation |
|----|----------|----------|-------------|---------|----------------|
| I1 | Inconsistency | MEDIUM | contracts/api.md `GET /api/bookmarks` vs `POST /bulk` & data-model.md | The browse list endpoint accepts only `tag` (include quick-filter); it does **not** accept `included_tags`/`excluded_tags`. Yet the bulk "matching" selector and the view-resolver (T048) honor excluded tags. So in normal browsing, an *excluded-tag* filter is only reachable through an open saved view. | Clarify that "current view with excluded tags" is only produced by a saved view, and ensure the front-end passes `saved_view_id` (or the expanded query) to the bulk selector so the two stay aligned. Optionally add `excluded_tag` to GET. |
| U1 | Underspecification | MEDIUM | spec.md Assumptions vs plan.md/research §9/tasks T007-T008,T073 | The client's explicit "single shared collection, no hidden per-session profiles" guarantee lives only in the plan/research/tasks, not as a numbered FR in the spec (the source of truth). | Consider adding an FR (e.g., FR-042) to the spec so the guarantee is traceable from the spec, not just the plan. |
| U2 | Underspecification | LOW | spec.md FR-025 vs plan.md/data-model.md/tasks T048 | FR-025 says "matching the current search/filter (including off-screen matches)"; the stronger definition you requested (included+excluded tags, unread/archive view, open saved view, all pages) is elaborated only in plan/data-model/tasks. Consistent, but the spec text is thinner than the design. | Optionally tighten FR-025 wording to name the full view components, so spec matches design. |
| O1 | Ordering | LOW | tasks.md Phase 8 (US6, P1) after Phases 6–7 (US4/US5, P2) | US6 "Powerful search" is priority **P1** but is sequenced (Phase 8) after two **P2** stories. Rationale exists (US5 tags feed `#tag`), and the Dependencies/MVP section correctly groups US1+US2+US3+US6 as the core loop. | Acceptable; the MVP note already resolves it. No change required, or move US6 earlier if strict priority ordering is preferred. |

## Implementation complete — all 14 stories built and verified

**All 77 tasks marked `[X]` in `tasks.md`.** The Bookmark Manager is running at `http://maker:4000` (review) / `http://127.0.0.1:4000` (capture), declared in `/work/.harness/app.json`.

### Verification results
- **Unit + integration:** `npm test` → **37/37 passing** (URL normalization/FR-041, search parser incl. quoted-operators-literal & malformed→error, sanitizer, tag reuse, import/export merge, save/edit, duplicate detection, archive isolation, bulk over the complete view, saved-view bulk, and the **5,000-bookmark bulk perf check (~138ms, well under 10s)**, plus restart persistence).
- **End-to-end (Playwright 1.61.0):** **4/4 passing** — load+readiness, save/search/open, archive round-trip, and bulk "select all matching".
- **Live API smoke tests:** create, duplicate→409, invalid→400, boolean search, malformed→400, tag suggest, preferences, export, bulk count/guard, import merge, saved views, preservation, archive — all correct.
- **Fresh server confirmed:** empty state renders and sets `data-harness-ready="true"`; defaults 25/medium.

### What was built (Node 24 + Express + SQLite, dependency-light SPA)
Every FR is implemented: rich-metadata save with editable title/description/**address**; duplicate-opens-existing (incl. archived restore) via strict FR-041 normalization; formatted sanitized notes; tag suggestions; advanced search; read/unread + unread view; reversible archiving; **bulk over the complete current view (search + included/excluded tags + view + open saved view, all pages) with exact pre-delete count**; sorting; saved views; preservation (self-contained HTML, PDF, Internet Archive); Netscape import/export with predictable merge; display preferences; and the **single shared collection** guaranteed across restarts/visits.

### Two things to flag honestly
1. **Front-end file layout differs from the task list.** Tasks named per-feature JS files (`editor.js`, `list.js`, `bulk.js`, …); I consolidated the client into `src/public/js/app.js` + `api.js`. All the *functionality* of those tasks is delivered and e2e-verified — only the file split differs.
2. **Two dependency deviations from the plan**, both to make it actually run/verify here: `better-sqlite3` was upgraded from v11 to **v13** (v11 hit a fatal SIGABRT at test teardown on Node 24), and the test runner uses single-process isolation. The pinned **Playwright 1.61.0** was preserved as specified.

Per SDD, these were fidelity-level implementation choices (they don't change approved behavior), so the spec/plan didn't need re-gating — but I'm surfacing them so you can decide if you'd like the front-end split into the originally-named modules or the dependency choices revisited.
